 Former Ohio State head coach Urban Meyer reportedly seriously considering a return to coaching at an unexpected Big Ten school
 A shocking development that no one could have pictured with Urban Meyer considering a return to coaching in the college world. 
 Brandon Little — 
 Ohio State Buckeyes & Cleveland Browns News Writer 
 Nov 18, 2026 10:14 AM EST 
 Jan 9, 2026; Atlanta, GA, USA; Urban Meyer on the sidelines prior to the 2025 Peach Bowl and semifinal game of the College Football Playoff between the Oregon Ducks and the Indiana Hoosiers at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images 
 When Urban Meyer left Ohio State in 2018 and handed the keys to Ryan Day, many people thought he was done with coaching. Meyer then landed with the Jacksonville Jaguars for the 2021 season, and that stint didn’t even last a full year. The thought was that his time in Columbus was his last run in college football.
 Now Meyer could be contemplating a return to coaching, and it’s with a Big Ten program that would put him right back in Ohio State’s world.
 Urban Meyer is in the mix for the Maryland job
 According to InsideMDSports of 247Sports , Meyer is emerging in Maryland’s search for its next head football coach. The report states Meyer has talked to Maryland athletic director Jim Smith about the job and is seriously considering it.
 Meyer and Smith have a past together. Smith once ran Ohio State’s Alumni Association, which helps explain how the two got connected on this opening.
 Big Ten · CFP No. 14 Ohio State Buckeyes 7-3 · 5-2 Big Ten · Projected 8.4 wins CFB Playoff

 Meyer is currently working in TV with Fox. A return to the sideline would give him a chance to end his coaching career on a better note than the one he had with the Jaguars. Jacksonville fired Meyer during the season, and that chapter has hung over his resume ever since.
 His name is a shocking addition to the Terrapins’ search following their in season firing of Mike Locksley. Maryland’s coaching search had previously centered on names like former LSU and Notre Dame head coach Brian Kelly, as well as Memphis coach Charles Huff.
 Meyer’s resume speaks for itself
 Meyer is one of the most decorated college football coaches ever. He won three national championships, two of them with Florida in 2006 and 2008 and another with Ohio State in 2014.
 While with the Buckeyes, Meyer also won three Big Ten championships, including titles in 2014 and 2017. He holds an overall record of 187-32 as a college head coach.
 There’s no questioning what Meyer has done on the field. The bigger question is how he would handle the job in its current form. Meyer is 62 years old, and he has not coached in the NIL era, which has all but changed how college football is run. Roster building, retention, and recruiting look a lot different than they did when he walked away from Ohio State.
 That makes this a big decision for Meyer. Taking over a program like Maryland in this landscape would be a far different challenge than the ones he faced in Gainesville and Columbus.
 What it would mean for Ohio State
 If Meyer ends up as Maryland’s next head coach, the move would have an impact on the Buckeyes. Ohio State would be set to go up against its former coach in conference play in some seasons, which would make for one of the more unique matchups on the Big Ten schedule.
 The impact wouldn’t stop on the field, either. Day and the Buckeyes would also find themselves recruiting against Meyer, a coach who built a large chunk of his reputation on the recruiting trail and knows exactly how Ohio State operates.
 This is quite the shocking development, and Meyer looks to be firmly in the mix in College Park. Whether he decides to step away from the TV booth and jump back into coaching remains to be seen, but the coming weeks will tell us whether a Meyer reunion with the game of college football is on the way.
